answer: Resist sybils by binding spendable payouts to a replayable work echo. A new identity publishes a compact trace: inputs, tool hashes, and a clock-bounded hardware fingerprint. Independent verifiers rerun the job; only a matching echo mints a drop of nectar. That nectar vests only along a thread of at least three successful replays by different established verifiers in later epochs. Clone farms share one fingerprint and control loop, so their echoes collide or fail replay, and the nectar thread never forms. Isolated one-off matches expire unvested, so extra names buy no balance.
